title: What If You Freefall in an Elevator?
sources: MIT Department of Physics, Elevator Freefall and Impact Dynamics
Center for Science in the Public Interest, Survival Physics in High Acceleration
Discovery Channel Mythbusters, Elevator Freefall Jump Test

lines.text: What happens if your elevator snaps and plunges into a freefall?
Most people believe jumping right before impact will cancel the speed and save you.
But physics says this is completely impossible.
The elevator is falling at fifty miles an hour, while you can only jump up at two miles an hour.
lines.caps: Falling at *50 MPH | you only jump *2 MPH | into the *floor

lines.text: Plus, jumping up will slam your head directly into the descending ceiling.
If you try standing with bent knees, the sheer G force will snap your legs and shatter your spine.
lines.caps: Standing with *bent knees | snaps your *legs | shatters your *spine

lines.text: The only real way to survive is to lie flat on your back in the center of the floor.
lines.caps: To *survive | lie *flat on your back | on the *floor

lines.text: This spreads the catastrophic impact evenly across your entire body and shields your vital organs.
lines.caps: This *spreads the impact | across your *entire body | shields vital *organs

lines.text: Never jump in an elevator, always lie flat.
